summary: Polk County, Florida lookout named only in the Forest Lookouts listing; a 2011 public auction sale for $505 is the one dated fact; no source describes the site now.

events.note: Sold at public auction for $505, per the Forest Lookouts entry

evidence.supports: Dated fact: tower sold at public auction in 2011 for $505
evidence.quote: 2011: The tower was sold at public auction for the sum of $505.00.

evidence.supports: Florida selling off aging manned towers; costs to taxpayers
evidence.quote: Over the past several years, the Division of Forestry says the towers, some around 70 years old, are costing taxpayers, in some cases, tens of thousands of dollars a year to maintain.
Technology has taken over for manned fire towers and the towers themselves are being sold off.

evidence.supports: Dismantled Leesburg tower won at auction by a Georgia man for about $600 who paid to take it apart
evidence.quote: The recently-dismantled Leesburg tower was won in an auction by a Georgia man, who paid about $600 for it and foot the bill to take it apart.

sources.title: Fla. Fire Towers Being Sold Off

notes_for_editor: Confidence low. The only source that names this tower is the Forest Lookouts listing, which gives a county and a 2011 auction sale for $505, and nothing else (no build date, height, design, staffing or site description). The 2010 WFTV report is statewide context and does not name this tower. Neither the cached NHLR nor the cached FFLOS Florida index lists a Pierce tower. Two searches found no other Pierce tower. One search snippet tied the name to the former phosphate-mining town of Pierce near Mulberry (an hmdb marker, not read); that may be where the name comes from, but no source links it to the tower. The record coordinates (27.7328, -81.9008) are from the Forest Lookouts listing and were not checked elsewhere. Do not merge this record with us-fl-lake-pierce-hatchinea-catfish-creek, which is a different register-listed tower. Page reads: 3 (Pierce listing, Firehouse article, Lake Pierce Wikipedia article).
